guide_enrichment.narrative: Our slight disagreement with the market starts with how LSU’s early offensive production translates against Texas A&M. LSU averaged 586 yards across 89 plays per game through its first two contests, but our opponent-adjusted numbers are much less impressed with its passing efficiency and ability to create scoring opportunities. That matters against a Texas A&M defense that grades particularly well at preventing opponents from reaching scoring position. LSU also committed five turnovers, including four interceptions, so the early yardage did not always become clean offensive value.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is LSU’s passing game against Texas A&M’s pass defense. Sam Leavitt produced 574 passing yards and five rushing touchdowns through two games, but he also threw four interceptions. Texas A&M’s coverage profile represents a meaningful step up in our numbers, and LSU may need Leavitt to create without giving away possessions.

recent_game.fact: LSU improved to 2-0 with a 45-14 win over Louisiana Tech on September 12, scoring 28 unanswered points in the second half.
LSU held Louisiana Tech to 139 total yards, eight first downs and minus-4 rushing yards.
Sam Leavitt passed for 344 yards and one touchdown and rushed for three touchdowns against Louisiana Tech.
Linebacker TJ Dottery led LSU with nine tackles against Louisiana Tech, while edge Princewill Umanmielen recorded three sacks and four tackles for loss.

opponent_notes.fact: LSU is scheduled to host Texas A&M at Tiger Stadium on September 26, 2026, with kickoff scheduled for 6:30 p.m. CT on ABC.
Texas A&M was 2-0 and ranked No. 9 in the AP poll and No. 8 in the Coaches poll when this guide was issued.

quarterback.fact: Starting quarterback Sam Leavitt, a transfer from Arizona State, had completed 41 of 66 passes for 574 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions through two games while rushing for 135 yards and five touchdowns.
Leavitt ranked second in the SEC in total offense at 354.5 yards per game through LSU's first two games.
Leavitt's 344 passing yards and three rushing touchdowns against Louisiana Tech were both career highs.
Leavitt entered LSU with 20 starts at Arizona State, where the Sun Devils went 16-4 in his starts.

offensive_personnel.fact: LSU used the same offensive line in each of its first two games: Jordan Seaton at left tackle, Bo Bordelon at left guard, Braelin Moore at center, Aliou Bah at right guard and Weston Davis at right tackle.
Left tackle Jordan Seaton and right guard Aliou Bah were among 13 transfers who made their first LSU starts in the season opener.
Center Braelin Moore started all 13 games for LSU in 2025, played 623 offensive snaps and allowed one sack.
Running back Dilin Jones led LSU through two games with 179 rushing yards and two touchdowns.

Tight end Trey'Dez Green had 10 receptions for 162 yards and one touchdown through two games; eight of his receptions produced either a first down or touchdown, and both of his direct-snap rushes produced first downs.
LSU had 14 first-time starters in its uniform through two games, including 13 transfers and true freshman defensive tackle Deuce Geralds.

defensive_personnel.fact: LSU used the same defensive starting lineup in its first two games: Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross at edge, Stephiylan Green and Deuce Geralds at defensive tackle, Whit Weeks and TJ Dottery at linebacker, PJ Woodland and DJ Pickett at cornerback, Tamarcus Cooley at free safety, Ty Benefield at rover and Dashawn Spears at star.
Umanmielen led the nation through two games with five sacks and 6.5 tackles for loss.
TJ Dottery led LSU with 14 tackles through two games, followed by Whit Weeks with 13.
LSU returned three starters from its 2025 secondary—cornerbacks PJ Woodland and DJ Pickett and safety Tamarcus Cooley—from a defense that recorded 17 interceptions and allowed 14 touchdown passes.
Transfer safety Ty Benefield entered LSU with 33 career starts and 235 tackles from Boise State.

coaching_changes.fact: Lane Kiffin is in his first season as LSU's head coach after being hired on November 30, 2025; LSU was 2-0 under him when the guide was issued.
Charlie Weis Jr. is LSU's first-year offensive coordinator and operates from the press box.
Blake Baker remained LSU's defensive coordinator, while first-year assistant Chris Kiffin was listed as co-defensive coordinator and linebackers coach.
Eric Wolford is LSU's first-year offensive line coach, and James Cregg serves as run-game specialist for the offensive line.

offensive_context.fact: LSU totaled 1,172 yards through two games, averaging 586.0 total yards, 358.0 passing yards and 228.0 rushing yards per game.
LSU ran 178 offensive plays through two games, an average of 89 per game, and averaged 6.6 yards per play.
LSU converted 19 of 33 third downs, scored on 12 of 14 red-zone trips and averaged 35:10 of possession through two games.
LSU rushed for 456 yards and eight touchdowns in its first two games; the Tigers did not reach either total until later in the 2025 season.
LSU outscored its first two opponents 27-3 in the first quarter.
LSU had committed five turnovers through two games, including four interceptions, and had a minus-one turnover margin.

defensive_context.fact: LSU allowed 284 total yards through two games, averaging 142.0 yards allowed per game, including 18.0 rushing and 124.0 passing.
LSU recorded 12 sacks and 22 tackles for loss through two games.
Opponents converted four of 27 third downs against LSU and failed on both fourth-down attempts through two games.
LSU forced 13 three-and-outs on 28 opponent possessions, and 22 of those possessions lasted four plays or fewer.
Only 14 of LSU's first 103 defensive snaps occurred in LSU territory, including six snaps on drives that began there following a turnover.
In 28 games under defensive coordinator Blake Baker, LSU allowed 26 passing touchdowns; it allowed one through the first two games of 2026.

special_teams.fact: Kicker Scott Starzyk was 4-for-5 on field goals and 10-for-10 on extra points through two games.
Starzyk made field goals from 25 and 23 yards against Louisiana Tech.
LSU averaged 37.4 yards per punt and 37.0 net yards per punt through two games.

series_context.fact: Texas A&M defeated LSU 49-25 on October 25, 2025, in the final game of Brian Kelly's LSU tenure.
LSU will host Texas A&M in Tiger Stadium for a second consecutive season.

other_relevant.fact: LSU's 2026 transfer class included quarterback Sam Leavitt, offensive tackle Jordan Seaton and edge Princewill Umanmielen, each identified by the guide as the top portal player at his position.
Thirty-five transfers appeared for LSU during the first two games of the season.
